name: LED

claims.claim_text: An LED is a solar cell operated in reverse: charge is injected and recombines, emitting photons. Absorption and emission are reciprocal and both are set by the material's bandgap, so a material that absorbs light efficiently is a candidate emitter.
claims.quote_verbatim: an LED, for example, is just a solar cell run in reverse
claims.speaker: Sam Stranks

claims.claim_text: Bright blue and green emission arrived with gallium nitride and displaced the dim silicon-carbide blue LEDs that preceded it; white LEDs followed shortly after, and the whole change reached the surplus and hobbyist market within a very short time.
claims.quote_verbatim: before that it was for blue LEDs, it was silicon carbide
claims.episode_title: Moore's Law, GaN and SiC devices - Gallimaufry GaN Gabble

claims.claim_text: LEDs tolerate a high defect density in the substrate, which is why usable gallium nitride LEDs were possible long before the same material was good enough for lasers or radio-frequency devices; substrate defect density was the limiting problem for those other applications.
claims.quote_verbatim: they still work really well if there's a high defect density in the substrate
claims.episode_title: Moore's Law, GaN and SiC devices - Gallimaufry GaN Gabble

claims.claim_text: Blue LEDs and solid-state lighting rest on a narrow physical accident: magnesium in gallium nitride happens to sit close enough to the valence band to act as a shallow acceptor and generate enough holes for p-type conduction. The doping that the whole industry depends on very nearly does not work.
claims.quote_verbatim: Magnesium and gallium nitride only accidentally behaves as a shallow acceptor

claims.claim_text: One manufacturer built LEDs on silicon carbide rather than the industry-standard substrates, using silicon carbide emitting layers for seven years from 1988 and then moving to more efficient nitride layers grown on silicon carbide, which remained its distinguishing process.
claims.quote_verbatim: from 1988 to 1995, so for seven years, we made silicon carbide on silicon carbide-based LEDs
claims.speaker: John Edmond
claims.episode_title: An Interview with John Edmond - Luciferous LED Lucubrator

claims.claim_text: Blue LEDs sold for about seventy-five dollars each in 1987 and were barely visible; the first competing silicon-carbide parts came in under a dollar, cutting the price by nearly two orders of magnitude at a stroke.
claims.quote_verbatim: they were $75 a piece and you could barely see them
claims.speaker: John Edmond
claims.episode_title: An Interview with John Edmond - Luciferous LED Lucubrator

claims.claim_text: A white LED is a blue LED behind a phosphor, which is why the properties of the blue emitter and of the phosphor together determine the spectrum of every white lighting product.
claims.quote_verbatim: a white LED is just a blue LED with a phosphor

claims.claim_text: Combining a phosphor-converted blue emitter with a separate red LED in the same fixture produces a spectrum whose colour rendering approaches an incandescent lamp, at the cost of two different emitters in one product.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's got a blue and a red and a phosphor
claims.speaker: John Edmond
claims.episode_title: An Interview with John Edmond - Luciferous LED Lucubrator

claims.claim_text: Colour rendering index measures how evenly a source covers the visible spectrum against the near-continuous spectrum of a filament lamp. Cheap white LEDs peak at particular wavelengths and lack others entirely, and binning for high colour rendering is what a professional lighting panel's price buys.
claims.quote_verbatim: color rendering index is an index from zero to a hundred
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Compact fluorescent lamps rate around 50 on that scale, peaking strongly in the green, because the light is produced by a phosphor coating rather than by a broadband emitter; different lamp technologies are distinguishable at a distance by their colour cast for the same reason.
claims.quote_verbatim: you showed like a CFL as like having 50 as a CRI

claims.claim_text: Commercially available LED bins reached about 170 lumens per watt, roughly twice the efficacy of the best compact fluorescent lamps of the time.
claims.quote_verbatim: our highest bins is about 170 lumens per watt
claims.speaker: John Edmond
claims.episode_title: An Interview with John Edmond - Luciferous LED Lucubrator

claims.claim_text: LED efficiency improves by a few percent per generation, with about a year between generations, so forecasts of a step change in efficiency over a few years are not supported by how the technology has actually advanced; the cumulative improvement over five or ten years is nonetheless large.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's a very slow incremental process to increase the efficiency
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Bob Pease, Jim Williams - Posthumous Pease Porridge

claims.claim_text: LEDs convert only twenty to thirty percent of their input power to light, so a high-power fixture must dissipate most of its rating as heat, and in installations where fans are unacceptable that thermal path constrains the whole design.
claims.quote_verbatim: LEDs are only like 30, 20, 30% efficient
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Heat is the dominant determinant of LED lifetime, so the design decision that matters most for a lighting product is the operating point: reducing dissipated power from five watts to two and a half can buy years of additional service, and the same part driven hard has a short life whatever its brand.
claims.quote_verbatim: heat is the main factor that kills the
claims.episode_title: Bob Pease, Jim Williams - Posthumous Pease Porridge

claims.claim_text: A hundred-thousand-hour LED is only as good as the driver behind it, and matching the electronics' lifetime to the emitter's is the harder half of the problem. In finished fixtures the driver is the component most likely to fail.
claims.quote_verbatim: the lead might have a lifetime of a hundred thousand hours or something, but can you design electronics to match that
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Low-cost LEDs frequently meet their headline lumens-per-watt figures when new and then fail within weeks, which is why practitioners designing lighting products buy only from the established manufacturers despite an order-of-magnitude price difference.
claims.quote_verbatim: they might meet their banner specs but they'll only meet it for a month
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Bob Pease, Jim Williams - Posthumous Pease Porridge

claims.claim_text: The older bulk-crystal red and green LEDs were extremely reliable; the blue, green and white parts that replaced them are thin-film devices and introduced failure modes that did not previously exist, so products designed on the assumption that LEDs do not fail have been caught out.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's based in thin film technology that is actually less reliable than the old LEDs
claims.episode_title: The King of Trash with Big Clive

claims.claim_text: Large-screen televisions drive their backlight LEDs hard enough that reducing the brightness setting on a new set materially extends its life, the alternative being a better and more expensive thermal design.
claims.quote_verbatim: the LEDs are being absolutely grilled in them
claims.episode_title: The King of Trash with Big Clive

claims.claim_text: Delivered LED assemblies can arrive largely non-functional; in one documented installation only seven of thirty units worked and the panels were installed anyway, knowing they did not work.
claims.quote_verbatim: Only seven of them out of 30 still work
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: The textbook figure of 20 milliamps for an indicator LED is far more current than modern parts need. In battery-powered equipment an indicator can be halved to a couple of milliamps by changing one resistor and remain perfectly visible, and at low total consumption that single component can dominate the current budget.
claims.quote_verbatim: they'll say, run your lead at 20 milliamps. Well, that's just bullshit
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: An LED continues to emit photons far below any practical drive current, measurably down into the tens of nanoamps and visibly in a dark room at a couple of microamps.
claims.quote_verbatim: the lead was still emitting photons down at, you know, like one microamp
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: At the extreme, the number of electrons needed to produce visible emission from an LED is of the order of a few hundred.
claims.quote_verbatim: I think it's a couple of hundred electrons required to light up a lead to any visible level
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Clap on, clap off, lights flicker

claims.claim_text: Indicator LEDs sized with a resistor chosen for the old 20 milliamp convention are blinding on modern parts, to the point of obscuring the LED beside them; ten kilohms is ample for an indicator that only has to be seen, not to light the room.
claims.quote_verbatim: I used way too low of a resistance value. And so the power LED is blinding
claims.speaker: Luke Valenty

claims.claim_text: Microcontroller and logic outputs carry two current limits: a per-pin maximum and a separate total limit on the ground or supply pin. A hundred-pin part rated at 30 milliamps per pin cannot source that from every pin at once, and multiplexing reduces the average current so that the total limit is respected even when the per-pin peak is not.
claims.quote_verbatim: they will have two specs for output current for each
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: LED Designs, Last Minute Designs and Board Designs

claims.claim_text: Older TTL logic families have enough output impedance to limit LED current on their own, and their high-level threshold of about two volts sits below the LED's roughly 2.2 volt forward drop, so an LED can be driven straight from the output. The technique is specific to that output stage and does not generalise to modern logic.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can stick an LED directly on the output of an LS chip with no current limiting resistor
claims.speaker: Ben Eater

claims.claim_text: A part sold as a single LED may be several dies in series inside one package, so a nominal 7.7 volt forward drop is a cluster of emitters rather than an unusual junction; the packaging hides a series arrangement that changes the drive circuit entirely.
claims.quote_verbatim: They're 7.7 volt leads
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: An instrument's diode-test range is bounded by its own supply: two cells give about three volts falling to a cutout near 2.1 volts, which is not enough to turn on some LEDs. Multimeters therefore often use three cells, both to reach the required test voltage and to use more of the battery capacity before cutting out.
claims.quote_verbatim: you've only got three volts max terminal voltage

claims.claim_text: LED output is close to linear with current while the eye's response is not, so a linear brightness ramp appears wrong. Squaring an eight-bit value and taking the top bits of the hardware's resolution is a good approximation to gamma correction; ten bits is barely enough and twelve is comfortable.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you take your eight-bit value, square it, and then use the top however many bits you've got in your hardware
claims.speaker: Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: Without gamma correction the lowest few dozen codes cover nearly the whole visible range of brightness while the top three quarters of the scale produce no perceptible change, which is what makes an uncorrected fade look wrong rather than merely imprecise.
claims.quote_verbatim: the first 32 codes sort of go from white
claims.speaker: Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: Looking at bare LEDs as point sources saturates the eye and hides differences between them; putting a diffuser over the same array makes colour-temperature variation between parts immediately visible. A display evaluated without its diffuser is therefore not evaluated at all.
claims.quote_verbatim: the eye tends to saturate
claims.speaker: Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: Ambient light levels indoors and in daylight differ by orders of magnitude, and the eye compensates so well that the difference is invisible without a light meter. A display signed off in a factory can be unusable once installed in a room with windows.
claims.quote_verbatim: Come to installing it, it goes in a corner office with windows on two sides. And guess what? It isn't bright enough
claims.speaker: Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: On a board carrying thousands of LEDs the current required for acceptable brightness is not known in advance and is far below the theoretical maximum, so sizing the supply for every LED at full output wastes cost and board area.
claims.quote_verbatim: if in theory these LEDs run at full blast could pull 20 amps, chances are you're not going to need that
claims.speaker: Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: Multiplexed LED arrays draw far more than their average current in the instant when a bank is lit, so a supply sized on average consumption browns out; a design lighting one sixteenth of its LEDs at a time still exceeded a 50 watt supply.
claims.quote_verbatim: When I had a five volt 10 amp supply that turned out not to be enough
claims.speaker: Jason Cerundolo

claims.claim_text: Dedicated LED matrix driver chips have historically been expensive and hard to obtain, which is why shift registers or a high pin-count microcontroller are the common alternatives for driving a row-column matrix.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can buy dedicated driver chips, but they're generally hard to get
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: LED Designs, Last Minute Designs and Board Designs

claims.claim_text: Addressable LEDs began as a separate controller chip in a small package that had to be wired to discrete LEDs and passives; integrating that controller into the LED package itself is what made long addressable strings practical.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's actually it's a controller chip

claims.claim_text: Before integration, each addressable pixel needed an LED, passives and an integrated circuit ganged together, which set a floor on pixel size and assembly effort. A package containing the RGB dies and the controller reduces a pixel to one part and a decoupling capacitor.
claims.quote_verbatim: when these guys put the SMD 50 50 package and then put the RGB in there with the controller
claims.speaker: Ryan O'Hara
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Ryan O'Hara - Keyed, Kerfed Kapton

claims.claim_text: Driving an LED matrix is an unusually good first FPGA project: it requires many pins driven in parallel to a demanding timing protocol, which is difficult on a microcontroller and natural in fabric where parallel units cost nothing, and it does not require the domain knowledge that other FPGA applications do.
claims.quote_verbatim: driving LED matrices is something that becomes pretty hairy when you use a microcontroller
claims.speaker: Claire Wolf

claims.claim_text: A shift-register matrix panel is built from sink drivers for the red, green and blue channels plus a row driver, all cascaded so the whole chain behaves as one long shift register with clock, data, latch and blank signals; panels then daisy-chain into a larger object.
claims.quote_verbatim: 16 bits multiplied by three because there are RGB LEDs
claims.speaker: Greg Davill

claims.claim_text: A large monochrome array is driven by combining a multi-channel PWM driver with multiplexing, and needs at least twelve bits of control per channel because gamma correction consumes most of the low end of the range.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's a 16-channel PWM driver and then an 8-to-1 multiplex
claims.speaker: Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: Where a board must exist in mirrored versions, mounting the driver ICs rotated rather than redrawing the layout is a legitimate shortcut at small quantities; only parts whose orientation matters electrically, such as MOSFETs and connectors, then need rework.
claims.quote_verbatim: I'll just mount all the drivers upside down
claims.speaker: Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: Assigning addresses to identical devices on a shared bus is straightforward; assigning them by physical position is not. A handheld probe that both issues the address command and senses contact can auto-increment as each node is touched, so an installer sets a starting address and then touches each unit in order.
claims.quote_verbatim: you send a command that says your address three and if you physically go and touch that particular one
claims.speaker: Mike Harrison
claims.episode_title: Live from Serbia with Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: On a large installation every cable and sub-assembly is tested with a purpose-built go/no-go jig before it goes up, because a fault in a section that has already been winched into place may require dismantling the parts installed after it. Building the jigs consumes an afternoon and is repaid immediately.
claims.quote_verbatim: I made a little box that you just plug in, it'll light up all the LEDs
claims.speaker: Mike Harrison
claims.episode_title: Live from Serbia with Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: LEDs are moisture-sensitive parts: absorbed water vaporises during reflow and can crack the package, so they are stored dry. Humidity also degrades the carrier tape itself, which sticks to the cover tape and jams feeders.
claims.quote_verbatim: LEDs do in particular hate the humidity
claims.speaker: Parker Dillman
claims.episode_title: An interview with Macrofab - Macro Manufacturing Mechanization

claims.claim_text: Pick-and-place placement pressure is a real hazard for LEDs, whose epoxy bodies break under excessive downward force; placement pressure is a machine setting that must be reduced for them.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can actually break them
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: LEDs with a recessed epoxy-filled cup can seal against the nozzle and refuse to release, a failure of the vacuum interface rather than of the placement itself; the fix is a different nozzle rather than more pressure.
claims.quote_verbatim: the pick and place just like won't let go of it

claims.claim_text: Carrier tape that is too thin lets parts bounce out as the feeder indexes. On a job requiring 22,000 LEDs, chosen because they were the only type in sufficient distributor stock, modifying the feeder reduced losses to about ten percent and one further reel had to be bought to cover the shortfall.
claims.quote_verbatim: the tape would advance and the LED would just bounce straight out of the tape
claims.speaker: Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: Reels carry enough parts that a product can stay in production for months on a single lot; when a new lot finally appears, forward voltage, current and intensity all shift together. A factory that records which reel built which board is what makes such a change diagnosable.
claims.quote_verbatim: forward voltage is different, current's different, intensity is different
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer

claims.claim_text: Substituting a cheaper addressable LED for a known-good part produced behaviour that three or four board revisions and vendor-suggested fixes, including adding a farad of capacitance, could not resolve; one vendor identified the parts as an obsolete revision of the internal controller that should no longer have been in circulation. The resolution was to accept a two-cent-per-LED increase and delay production.
claims.quote_verbatim: we're going to have to wait. We'll use the things that we know work
claims.speaker: Jesse Vincent

claims.claim_text: Building and checking a single panel before releasing the rest of a run catches orientation errors, which occur on essentially every build: on one board LEDs were placed upside down and a converter was rotated by 180 degrees.
claims.quote_verbatim: we'll populate one panel and then I'm just going to kind of make sure it's all good
claims.speaker: Jared Wolff

claims.claim_text: Sourcing region dominates LED cost at hobby and small-production volumes: the same order came to about thirty dollars from an overseas supplier against roughly 250 dollars for the nearest catalogue equivalent from a Western distributor, a difference of about eight times on the part price alone.
claims.quote_verbatim: I paid 0.007 cents per LED at the quantity I was buying

claims.claim_text: Lighting-class white LEDs in the common surface-mount formats cost under a cent each in reel quantities and are very bright, though installations intended to last are still specified with branded parts, which competition has also made inexpensive.
claims.quote_verbatim: If you buy a reel of those, they're under one cent each
claims.speaker: Mike Harrison
claims.episode_title: Live from Serbia with Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: Component count multiplies fast in LED-heavy designs: fifty LEDs on each of fifty thousand boards is two and a half million parts, a quantity few suppliers hold, so the lead time runs to at least twenty weeks and the part choice is frozen at the moment the order is placed.
claims.quote_verbatim: 50 LEDs times 50,000 boards

claims.claim_text: During the component shortage even ordinary through-hole indicator LEDs became unobtainable, with lead times of three to four months on parts that had always been available from stock.
claims.quote_verbatim: I couldn't get like LEDs, like really basic
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer

claims.claim_text: In a densely populated LED object the emitters and their drivers dominate the bill of materials at roughly sixty dollars each, while the bare circuit boards are effectively free by comparison and a rush-ordered 3D printed enclosure cost more than both together.
claims.quote_verbatim: I think it's about $60 worth of LEDs
claims.speaker: Greg Davill

claims.claim_text: Hand-populating LED panels runs at roughly a quarter of an hour per panel of 120 LEDs when panelised four at a time, which is what makes objects with thousands of LEDs feasible for one person but not repeatable.
claims.quote_verbatim: each four probably took maybe an hour
claims.speaker: Greg Davill

claims.claim_text: Setting up a pick-and-place machine whose feeders cannot be changed quickly costs more than a day of loading tape and recording feeder data, which rules it out for varied work. An LED matrix inverts that calculation, because one reel loaded once places thousands of identical parts.
claims.quote_verbatim: in the case of an LED matrix where there's only one part and suddenly it's really efficient
claims.episode_title: LEDs Everywhere with Tim from Mitxela

claims.claim_text: A panel of four boards each carrying 300 identical LEDs is 1,200 placements, which a three-head machine completes in roughly twenty minutes; identical-part boards are the case where machine placement is unambiguously worth the setup.
claims.quote_verbatim: 1,200 placements in a row

claims.claim_text: An LED works as a photodetector as well as an emitter, an idea documented and submitted to a corporate laboratory decades before the same technique appeared in a commercial product.
claims.quote_verbatim: using an LED as a light sensor is not something you'd normally think of
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer

claims.claim_text: Using LEDs as wavelength-selective detectors in a sun photometer avoids the optical filters that degrade over time. The two original LEDs in one instrument remained in service for 24 years measuring atmospheric optical depth at 880 and 940 nanometres, with total column water vapour derived from the same readings.
claims.quote_verbatim: I measure sunlight using light-emitting diodes instead of filters in front of photodiodes
claims.speaker: Forrest Mims
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Forrest Mims - Snell Solisequious Scientist

claims.claim_text: LED detector stability is not uniform across a batch: in a seven-LED instrument some drifted over ten years while others did not, so long-term instruments carry several channels and the drifting ones are identified and discarded.
claims.quote_verbatim: A couple of them have drifted. But two or three of them are just as stable as a rock after 10 years
claims.speaker: Forrest Mims
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Forrest Mims - Snell Solisequious Scientist

claims.claim_text: Because one LED can both emit and detect, a bidirectional optical link can be built over a single fibre with one device at each end rather than a separate emitter and detector pair.
claims.quote_verbatim: an LED that emits light with a modulated voice or signal is the same LED that detects the light
claims.speaker: Forrest Mims
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Forrest Mims - Snell Solisequious Scientist

claims.claim_text: An indicator LED is an unintended data channel: it has enough bandwidth that firmware toggling it can be read optically with a phototransistor, extracting memory contents without opening the device.
claims.quote_verbatim: LEDs have a reasonable amount of bandwidth. So put a photo transistor on there and you can get a ROM dump
claims.speaker: Trammell Hudson

claims.claim_text: Imitation neon is white LEDs in a vinyl extrusion behind a coloured diffuser, which avoids the thousands of volts and the glass forming that genuine neon requires.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's basically like LEDs encased in like vinyl

claims.claim_text: Long-throw stage lighting still uses discharge lamps because the optics need the light generated in a very small area, which LEDs cannot match: spreading emission over a larger area is inherent to the technology and the concentrated source cannot tolerate the temperatures involved.
claims.quote_verbatim: all that light has been generated in a very tiny area, which is completely incompatible with LED technology
claims.episode_title: The King of Trash with Big Clive

claims.claim_text: Bringing every register bit, latch and state-machine output to an LED turns a processor into an inspectable object: single-stepping through code then shows the entire machine state at each step.
claims.quote_verbatim: all of the registered states were shown on the front in LEDs
claims.episode_title: Picking a Pick and Place Pickiness

claims.claim_text: A power indicator LED and a second LED on a spare digital output are among the cheapest and most useful additions to a board. Their absence is a recurring omission, and their presence distinguishes at a glance between a board that is unpowered, a board whose supply is being back-fed through an I/O pin, and a board that is running.
claims.quote_verbatim: I didn't put an LED, just an indicator LED for power

claims.claim_text: Adding a few lines of code to blink an LED or toggle a pin, then observing it, remains a sufficient debugging technique for a large class of firmware problems and needs no instrument beyond an oscilloscope probe.
claims.quote_verbatim: actually blinks a lead or does a serial output or toggles a line
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Practical firmware debugging uses a mixture of techniques rather than one: a serial terminal for output, indicator LEDs for state, and a hardware debugger for stepping, each suited to a different class of problem and to different timing constraints.
claims.quote_verbatim: having LEDs available, having a printf out to a, out to a serial terminal, like that's all really important

claims.claim_text: Measuring an LED's luminous output to compute the exact drive current is engineering that most designs do not need: the resistor is adjusted after the board is built and the brightness is judged in place. Where the LEDs are the product rather than an indicator, the opposite holds and the drive must be engineered from the start.
claims.quote_verbatim: most designers are content just to change the resistor value after the fact
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Selecting LEDs on price against light output for a given package is poorly served by parametric search, and practitioners who do it often work from a remembered set of favourite parts built up over many projects rather than re-selecting each time.
claims.quote_verbatim: that had come down with the experience of doing 20 different LED projects

claims.claim_text: LED driver controllers from minor manufacturers may have no public datasheet, and a datasheet found elsewhere bearing exactly the same part number can describe a different package and part, so the identification cannot be trusted without corroboration.
claims.quote_verbatim: I realized this isn't the right part, even though the part number is exact
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: LED strip is mounted into an aluminium profile with thermally conductive double-sided tape, which is the strip's heat path rather than a mounting convenience; ordinary double-sided tape in its place removes the cooling.
claims.quote_verbatim: You actually stick them down with a thermal adhesive tape
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: At 0201 size the polarity marking on an LED is at the limit of what can be seen while placing it, and a 3D printed jig matching the board outline to hold it flat is what makes hand assembly at that size practical.
claims.quote_verbatim: I successfully saw the dot on the O2O1 LED

claims.claim_text: Producing a visible physical change is what converts curiosity into sustained interest in electronics, which is why blinking an LED functions as the discipline's equivalent of a first program and why the next step is usually to drive something larger.
claims.quote_verbatim: It is just critical that you can impart some kind of change on your environment with electronics
claims.episode_title: Distribution, Wozniak & Robots - Early Eight-bit Endgame

claims.claim_text: A beginner needs an endpoint that leads somewhere rather than a self-contained exercise: soldering a kit with no follow-on leaves the learner without a next step, while a platform that blinks an LED and can be extended provides one.
claims.quote_verbatim: finding something that's going to either make a motor move or is going to make an led blink
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Teaching from the top down works because each concept is introduced when a project demands it: transistors become necessary when the LED to be driven exceeds what a logic output can supply, and the underlying physics becomes interesting only after the device has been used enough to raise the question.
claims.quote_verbatim: You don't really need to understand. About transistors. Until you want to start driving. Bigger LEDs

claims.claim_text: Semiconductor physics becomes tractable once the learner has enough experience with the device to have formed the questions, which is the reverse of the order most curricula use.
claims.quote_verbatim: Once you've used an led enough to be like, Oh, why is it 0.7 volts?

claims.claim_text: An LED, a battery and a resistor are enough to produce the sense of discovery that motivates learning; a full development platform is not a prerequisite and can obscure what is happening.
claims.quote_verbatim: you could do that with LED and a battery and a resistor
claims.speaker: Saar Drimer

claims.claim_text: Demonstrations built from an LED and improvised parts, such as a battery made from a silver coin, a piece of magnesium and acidified paper, hold an audience's attention regardless of their background, and cost nothing.
claims.quote_verbatim: you light up an LED with that little homemade battery
claims.speaker: Forrest Mims
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Forrest Mims - Snell Solisequious Scientist

claims.claim_text: Reaching for a microcontroller to flash an LED where a timer chip would serve is common practice; the simpler circuit does the same job and is more instructive about how it works.
claims.quote_verbatim: people will use a micro or an Arduino, for example, to build a little flasher when they could just use the 555
claims.speaker: Forrest Mims
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Forrest Mims - Snell Solisequious Scientist
